notes:
On Linux, Corylus now notices when a document is edited by another program. It never did: a file's own closing was overwriting the record of the write that preceded it, so the change was discarded before anything was told about it. This affected Linux only — on macOS and Windows external edits have always been picked up.

- Search can find your writing again: saving a document was erasing its text from the search index a fraction of a second after writing it, so searching only ever matched titles and synopses. Every affected document is re-indexed automatically the next time the project opens.
- Fixed a bug that could make Corylus read a document as if it had no title, no synopsis and no identity at all, and then treat it as a different document. Whether it happened depended on where the accented letters fell in the text.
- Documents can no longer disappear from the binder while their file sits safely on disk. Affected projects repair themselves on open.
- A document moved into a folder could stop being found by search, because its entry still pointed at the folder it came from.
